tex_content.html:
\begin{claim} \end{claim}[Dirichlet problem on small geodesic balls] ↗ def:exponential-map ↗ cor:exponential-local-diffeomorphism ↗ lem:laplacian-local-formula

For every $p$ in an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold there is $r_D(p)>0$ such that, for $0<s\le r_D(p)$:

  1. $\exp _p$ identifies $B(0,s)\subset T_pM$ diffeomorphically with $B(p,s)$, identifies their closures, and identifies the boundary with the smooth metric sphere $S(p,s)\cong S^{n-1}$;

  2. every continuous $\varphi \colon S(p,s)\to \Ar $ has a continuous extension $h$ to $\overline B(p,s)$ which is smooth and harmonic in $B(p,s)$.

The normal-ball assertion follows from the exponential-map theory in \cite{doCarmo}; the Dirichlet assertion is the standard local elliptic result used in \cite{Petersen}. \end{claim}
